# miniflux on the k3s cluster (3x pi 4 + the old thinkpad as the "big" node)
# apply with:   envsubst < miniflux.yaml | kubectl apply -f -
# needs MINIFLUX_DB_PASSWORD and MINIFLUX_ADMIN_PASSWORD exported in the shell first
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: miniflux
  labels: {app.kubernetes.io/part-of: reading, homelab/backup: "true"}
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: miniflux-secrets
  namespace: miniflux
type: Opaque
stringData:
  DATABASE_URL: "postgres://miniflux:${MINIFLUX_DB_PASSWORD}@miniflux-db:5432/miniflux?sslmode=disable"
  ADMIN_USERNAME: "admin"
  ADMIN_PASSWORD: ${MINIFLUX_ADMIN_PASSWORD}
  POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${MINIFLUX_DB_PASSWORD}
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
    name: miniflux-config
    namespace: miniflux
data:
    RUN_MIGRATIONS: "1"
    CREATE_ADMIN: "1"
    POLLING_FREQUENCY: "30"        # minutes
    BATCH_SIZE: '50'
    BASE_URL: "https://rss.home.example.net/"
    LOG_DATE_TIME: "true"
    CLEANUP_ARCHIVE_READ_DAYS: "90"
    # postgres tuning for a pi with 4GB, copied from pgtune and then halved because it OOMed once
    postgresql.conf: |
        shared_buffers = 128MB
        effective_cache_size = 512MB
        work_mem = 4MB
        max_connections = 20
        # keep WAL small, the USB SSD thanks you
        wal_compression = on
        max_wal_size = 256MB
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: miniflux-db-data
  namespace: miniflux
  annotations:
    # 2 replicas, the third node is the thinkpad and it goes to sleep sometimes
    longhorn.io/number-of-replicas: "2"
spec:
  accessModes: [ "ReadWriteOnce" ]
  storageClassName: longhorn
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 5Gi
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata:
  name: miniflux-db
  namespace: miniflux
  labels: &db_labels
    app: miniflux
    component: db
spec:
  serviceName: miniflux-db
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels: *db_labels
  template:
    metadata:
      labels: *db_labels
    spec:
      nodeSelector: { kubernetes.io/arch: arm64 }
      containers:
      - name: postgres
        image: postgres:16-alpine
        args: ["-c", "config_file=/etc/postgresql/postgresql.conf"]
        env:
        - name: POSTGRES_USER
          value: miniflux
        - name: POSTGRES_PASSWORD
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef: {name: miniflux-secrets, key: POSTGRES_PASSWORD}
        - {name: PGDATA, value: /var/lib/postgresql/data/pgdata}
        ports:
        - containerPort: 5432
          name: postgres
        readinessProbe:
          exec:
            command: [ "pg_isready", "-U", "miniflux" ]
          initialDelaySeconds: 10
          periodSeconds:   10
        volumeMounts:
        - {name: data, mountPath: /var/lib/postgresql/data}
        - name: config
          mountPath: /etc/postgresql/postgresql.conf
          subPath: postgresql.conf
      volumes:
      - name: data
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: miniflux-db-data
      - name: config
        configMap:
          name: miniflux-config
          items: [{key: postgresql.conf, path: postgresql.conf}]
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: miniflux
  namespace: miniflux
  labels: &web_labels {app: miniflux, component: web}
spec:
  replicas: 1
  revisionHistoryLimit: 3
  strategy:
    type: Recreate
  selector:
    matchLabels: *web_labels
  template:
    metadata:
      labels: *web_labels
      annotations:
        # bump this to force a restart after editing the configmap
        homelab/restarted-at: "2024-06-02T21:14:00Z"
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: miniflux
          image: "miniflux/miniflux:2.1.3"
          ports:
            - containerPort: 8080
              name: http
          envFrom:
            - configMapRef: {name: miniflux-config}
            - secretRef:
                name: miniflux-secrets
          resources:
            requests: {cpu: 50m, memory: "64Mi"}
            limits:
              memory: 256Mi
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet: {path: /healthcheck, port: http}
            initialDelaySeconds: 15
            failureThreshold: 3
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata: {name: miniflux, namespace: miniflux}
spec:
  selector:
    app: miniflux
    component: web
  ports:
    - {name: http, port: 80, targetPort: http}
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: miniflux
  namespace: miniflux
  annotations:
    cert-manager.io/cluster-issuer: "letsencrypt-prod"
    traefik.ingress.kubernetes.io/router.entrypoints: websecure
    traefik.ingress.kubernetes.io/router.middlewares: "kube-system-lan-only@kubernetescrd,kube-system-secure-headers@kubernetescrd"
    homelab/notes: >-
      Only reachable from the LAN and over tailscale. If you are reading this
      because the cert expired again, check that the DNS-01 token in the cert-manager namespace hasn't been rotated.
spec:
  ingressClassName: traefik
  tls:
  - hosts: [rss.home.example.net]
    secretName: miniflux-tls
  rules:
  - host: rss.home.example.net
    http:
      paths:
      - path: /
        pathType: Prefix
        backend:
          service:
            name: miniflux
            port: {name: http}
---
# TODO: network policy so only traefik can talk to miniflux, and only miniflux to the db
# apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
# kind: NetworkPolicy
# metadata:
#   name: miniflux-db-only-from-web
---
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: miniflux-db-backup
  namespace: miniflux
spec:
  schedule: "30 3 * * *"
  concurrencyPolicy: Forbid
  successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 1
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      backoffLimit: 2
      template:
        spec:
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
          containers:
          - name: pg-dump
            image: postgres:16-alpine
            command: ["/bin/sh", "-c"]
            args:
              - |
                set -eu
                FILE=/backup/miniflux-$(date +%Y%m%d).sql.gz
                pg_dump -h miniflux-db -U miniflux miniflux | gzip > "$FILE"
                find /backup -name 'miniflux-*.sql.gz' -mtime +14 -delete
            env:
              - name: PGPASSWORD
                valueFrom: {secretKeyRef: {name: miniflux-secrets, key: POSTGRES_PASSWORD}}
            volumeMounts: [{name: backup, mountPath: /backup}]
          volumes:
          - name: backup
            nfs: {server: 192.168.1.20, path: /volume1/k3s-backups/miniflux}
...

openapi: "3.0.3"
info:
  title: sprout
  version: '0.4.1'
  # fmt: markdown
  description: "Tiny HTTP API for the balcony watering controller (a Pi Zero 2 W, four 12V solenoid valves and some capacitive soil moisture sensors that are *mostly* calibrated).\n\nEverything runs on the LAN. There's no auth beyond an API key because the only clients are Home Assistant and my phone.\n\n- moisture values are percentages, 0 = bone dry, 100 = sitting in a cup of water\n- times are UTC unless a field says otherwise\n"
  contact: {name: Ines, url: "https://github.com/inesferreira/sprout"}
  license:
    name: MIT
servers:
  - url: http://{host}:{port}/api/v1
    description: "on the LAN"
    variables:
      host: { default: sprout.lan }
      port:
        default: "8000"
        enum: ["8000", "80"]

tags:
- name: zones
  description: Watering zones (one valve each)
- name: sensors
- name: schedule
  description: >-
    Cron-ish schedules. The controller skips a scheduled run if the zone's moisture is already above its target, so you can be generous here.

security:
  - apiKey: []

# shared error responses, merged into every path below
x-error-responses: &errors
  '401': {$ref: '#/components/responses/Unauthorized'}
  '404': {$ref: '#/components/responses/NotFound'}

paths:
  /zones:
    get:
      tags: [zones]
      summary: List all zones
      operationId: listZones
      responses:
        '200':
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: array
                items: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Zone'}
              example:
                - {id: 1, name: "tomatoes", valve_gpio: 17, target_moisture: 45, state: idle}
                - {id: 2, name: herbs, valve_gpio: 27, target_moisture: 35, state: "watering"}
  /zones/{zoneId}:
    parameters:
      - $ref: '#/components/parameters/ZoneId'
    get:
      tags: [ zones ]
      summary: Get one zone
      operationId: getZone
      responses:
        "200":
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/Zone"
        <<: *errors
    patch:
      tags: [zones]
      summary: Update a zone
      description: Only the fields you send are changed. Sending `state` is not allowed, use the `/water` endpoint for that.
      operationId: updateZone
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/ZoneUpdate'}
      responses:
        '200':
          description: The updated zone
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: {$ref: "#/components/schemas/Zone"}
        '422':
          description: Validation error, e.g. target_moisture outside 0..100
        <<: *errors
  /zones/{zoneId}/water:
    parameters:
    - $ref: '#/components/parameters/ZoneId'
    post:
      tags: [zones]
      summary: Water a zone now
      operationId: waterZone
          # fmt: markdown
      description: |
        Opens the zone's valve and starts the pump.
        * returns immediately (`202`), poll `GET /zones/{zoneId}` to see when it's done
        * if moisture is already above target this is a no-op unless `force` is true
        * the pump also has a hard 10 minute timeout in firmware, belt and braces
      requestBody:
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: object
              properties:
                seconds:
                  type: integer
                  minimum: 1
                  maximum: 600
                  default: 30
                  description: How long to open the valve for. Capped at 10 minutes because I flooded the downstairs neighbour's balcony once.
                force: {type: boolean, default: false, description: "Water even if moisture is above target"}
      responses:
        '202':
          description: Accepted, valve is opening
        '409':
          description: Another zone is already watering (the pump can only feed one valve at a time)
        <<: *errors
  /sensors/readings:
    get:
      tags: [sensors]
      summary: Recent moisture readings
      operationId: listReadings
      parameters:
        - name: zone
          in: query
          schema: {type: integer}
        - name: since
          in: query
          description: ISO 8601 timestamp, defaults to 24 hours ago
          schema:
            type: string
            format: date-time
          example: 2024-05-01T06:30:00Z
        - {name: limit, in: query, schema: {type: integer, default: 100, maximum: 1000}}
      responses:
        '200':
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: array
                items:
                  $ref: '#/components/schemas/Reading'

components:
  securitySchemes:
    apiKey:
      type: apiKey
      in: header
      name: X-Sprout-Key
  parameters:
    ZoneId:
      name: zoneId
      in: path
      required: true
      schema:
        type: integer
        minimum: 1
        maximum: 4
  responses:
    Unauthorized:
      description: Missing or wrong `X-Sprout-Key` header
    NotFound:
      description: "No such zone"
  schemas:
    Zone:
      type: object
      required: [id, name, valve_gpio, state]
      properties:
        id: {type: integer, readOnly: true}
        name:
          type: string
          maxLength: 32
        valve_gpio:
          type: integer
          description: BCM pin number, not the physical pin. Yes I mixed these up once. Yes the wrong valve opened.
        target_moisture: {type: integer, minimum: 0, maximum: 100, nullable: True}
        state:
          type: string
          enum: [idle, watering, cooldown, error, disabled]
        last_watered:
          type: string
          format: date-time
          nullable: true
          example: "2024-05-01T06:30:00Z"
        notes:
          type: string
          description: >+
            Free text, shown on the Home Assistant card.

    ZoneUpdate:
      type: object
      properties:
        name: {type: string, maxLength: 32}
        target_moisture: { type: integer, minimum: 0, maximum: 100 }
        enabled:
          type: boolean
      additionalProperties: false
    Reading:
      type: object
      properties:
        zone: {type: integer}
        at: {type: string, format: date-time}
        moisture: {type: number, format: float, example: 41.5}
        raw: {type: integer, description: Raw ADC value before calibration, example: 18234}
        battery_v:
          type: number
          example: 3.70
          deprecated: true
          description: |-
            Only the old ESP8266 sensor nodes report this.
            The wired ones on the Pi always return null.

Changelog
=========

All notable changes to **Tidy Chests** are documented here. The format is (loosely) based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/ "Keep a Changelog 1.1.0"), and the mod uses [semantic versioning](https://semver.org/), which for a Stardew mod mostly means "the major version goes up when I break your config".
If you're updating from 1.x, read the 2.0.0 notes first, *please*, it'll save us both a Nexus comment.  

## [Unreleased]

### Added
- Controller support for the sort button (finally!) — it's on <kbd>Right Stick</kbd> press by default and can be changed in GMCM
- Italian translation, thanks to _Giulia_ :it:
+ `sortJunimoChests` option, off by default because Junimo chests are shared between all of them and sorting them in multiplayer surprised a lot of people who were not expecting their stuff to move around while they were standing right there

### Fixed
* The fridge in the farmhouse no longer gets sorted into the mini-fridge (#87)
* Sorting a chest with exactly 36 items no longer drops the last item on the floor. Nobody lost anything valuable as far as I know, but if you did, sorry!!

## [2.1.0] - 2024-03-30 ##

### Added

- New sort mode **"by category, then quality"**, which is what most people asked for in the poll:
  1. category (crops, artisan goods, fish, ...)
  2. quality, iridium first
  3. name
- The GMCM page has a live preview now   

![the new sort button](docs/images/sort-button.png "The sort button, top right next to the colour picker")

### Changed

- The default hotkey moved from `S` to `Shift+S`, because `S` is also "move down" for about half of you. Yes, I should have thought about that in 1.0.
- ~~Chests are sorted when you open them~~ Chests are sorted when you __close__ them, so you can actually see what you're doing.

| Action | Old default | New default |
|---|:---:|---|
| Sort | `S` | `Shift+S` |
| Toggle auto-sort|none| `Shift+A` |
| Undo last sort | `Ctrl+Z` |`Ctrl+Z` (unchanged)|

### Removed

- The `legacySort` option. It's been deprecated since 1.6 and the code was getting in the way of everything else.

***

2.0.0 — 2024-01-14
------------------

:warning: **Breaking:** the config format changed. The mod migrates your old `config.json` automatically on first launch and keeps a backup as `config.json.bak`, but if you edited it by hand you might want to double check the result. Old vs. new:

~~~json
{ "SortKey": "S", "SortOnOpen": true, "IgnoredChests": ["Fridge"] }
~~~

```json
{
  "Hotkeys": { "Sort": "LeftShift + S" },
  "SortWhen": "Close",
  "Ignore": { "ChestNames": ["Fridge"], "Junimo": true }
}
```

When the migration runs you'll see this in the SMAPI console:

    [Tidy Chests] Migrated config.json (v1 -> v2), backup saved as config.json.bak
    [Tidy Chests] 3 ignored chest names carried over

#### Added
* Per-chest ignore: put `#nosort` anywhere in a chest's name, e.g. `Seeds #nosort`. Chest names ending in \* are treated the same way, for people who were already doing that with the old *Chest Labels* mod
* Compatibility with *Chests Anywhere* and *Automate*[^automate]

#### Fixed
* crash when sorting while a festival is loading (only on Android?)
* coloured chests losing their colour after sorting :bug:

Known issues that are still open, numbered the same as in the pinned Nexus post:

4. Sorting Ginger Island chests sometimes needs a second click
5. The GMCM preview is wrong for stacks over 999
7. Big chests (1.6) sort fine but the preview only shows the first 36 slots

## 1.6.2 - 2023-09-02
- fix: compatibility with SMAPI 3.18.5

--- title: "Contributing" weight: 90 draft: false aliases: [ /docs/contributing/, "/hacking/" ] description: "How to build teacup from source, run the tests, and get a pull request merged without too much back-and-forth. Please skim this before opening a big PR, it'll save us both time." --- # Contributing to teacup # First off: thanks for even opening this file! :tea: teacup is a one-person hobby project (hi, I'm Rosa) that somehow turned into a thing a few hundred people use for their blogs, and every bug report, typo fix, theme and PR genuinely helps. That said, I work on this in the evenings and at weekends, so please be patient if I don't reply for a week or two; it's not personal, I promise. Small PRs get merged faster than big ones. If you want to do something big, open an issue first so we can talk about it *before* you sink a weekend into it. Getting set up ============== You need: + Go 1.22 or newer + `make` (on Windows use WSL, or just run the commands from the `Makefile` by hand) + optionally [`watchexec`](https://github.com/watchexec/watchexec "watchexec on GitHub") for `make watch` Then: 1) fork the repo and clone your fork 2) `make build` — this produces `./bin/teacup` 3) `make test` — runs the unit tests *and* the golden-file tests in `testdata/sites/` 4) `./bin/teacup serve ./examples/blog` and open http://localhost:1313 If step 3 fails on a fresh clone, that's a bug. Please tell me! ## Project layout ```text cmd/teacup/ CLI entry point (cobra) internal/build/ the actual site builder internal/markdown/ goldmark setup + our extensions (callouts, footnotes, heading ids) internal/theme/ template loading; the default theme is in internal/theme/default/ testdata/sites/ golden-file tests, each folder is a tiny site + its expected output ``` ### Golden-file tests Each folder under `testdata/sites/` has a `site/` and an `expected/` directory. The test builds `site/` and diffs the output against `expected/`. When you change the output on purpose, regenerate the expected files with: UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 go test ./internal/build/... and then **look at the diff** before committing it. I have merged broken golden files before because I didn't look. Don't be me. ### Testing with a real site Most bugs only show up with real content, so it helps to test against a site with a config like this one (it turns on most of the optional features): ```yaml # teacup.yaml title: "Rosa's test blog" baseURL: http://localhost:1313/ theme: default paginate: 10 markdown: smartypants: true footnotes: yes callouts: [note, tip, warning, danger] taxonomies: { tags: tag, series: series } feeds: - {type: atom, path: /feed.xml, limit: 20} - type: json path: /feed.json build: drafts: false future: False minify: ~ ``` ## Commit messages & PRs I don't care much about commit message format, but please make the PR description useful. The template in `.github/pull_request_template.md` looks like this, fill it in and delete whatever doesn't apply: ````markdown ## What does this change? ## ## Checklist * [ ] `make test` passes * [ ] golden files updated (and I actually looked at the diff) * [ ] docs updated if behaviour changed + [ ] added myself to `CONTRIBUTORS.md` if I wanted to ```` ## Code style `gofmt` and `go vet` are enforced in CI, `golangci-lint` runs too but only as a warning for now. Beyond that: - keep functions short-ish; if you need to scroll, split it - errors: wrap them with `fmt.Errorf("doing X: %w", err)`, don't log *and* return - no new dependencies without asking first. teacup's whole point is being small: - the binary is ~9 MB and I'd like to keep it under 15 - `go.sum` currently has 23 lines, it was 210 before I dropped the second markdown library[^deps] > **A note on themes** > > Themes don't live in this repo anymore (except the default one). Publish yours as a separate repo with the `teacup-theme` topic and it'll show up on the [themes page][themes]. Please don't send PRs that add themes here, I'll politely close them. ### Makefile targets | target | what | notes| |--|--|--| | `make build` | build `./bin/teacup` | uses `-trimpath` | | `make test` | unit + golden tests | | | `make watch` | rebuild and re-serve the example blog on every change | needs watchexec | | `make release` | cross-compile for linux/mac/windows, amd64 + arm64 | **maintainers only**, needs `GITHUB_TOKEN` | ## Reporting bugs Please include the output of `teacup version`, your OS, and ideally a tiny site that reproduces the problem (a zip, or a link to a repo). "My site doesn't build" with no details makes me sad :cry:.
Why does teacup version print a git hash? Release builds embed the commit they were built from. If you see `(devel)` you built from source without `make`, which is fine, but tell me which commit you're on.
## Code of conduct Be kind. That's basically it. The longer version is in [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md); TL;DR: no harassment, no gatekeeping, assume good intent, and remember there's a human on the other end who's doing this for fun. --- _Thanks again for helping out_ — Rosa\ teacup is MIT licensed; by contributing you agree your code is too. [^deps]: Not because the library was bad! It was great. It just pulled in half of the internet for a feature (math rendering) that four people used, and those four people can use KaTeX on the client side. [themes]: https://teacup.example.dev/themes/ "Community themes"

romsort

Sort, rename and de-duplicate your ROM dumps using [No-Intro](https://no-intro.org "No-Intro dat-o-matic") and [Redump][redump] DAT files. Everything happens locally, nothing gets uploaded anywhere, and it never deletes a file unless you explicitly pass `--delete-dupes` **and** confirm. I wrote this because my "Retro" folder had grown to 40 GB of `Super Mario World (USA) (1).zip`, `smw_final_FINAL.sfc` and friends, and every existing tool either wanted a GUI, Windows, or both. [![Docs](https://img.shields.io/badge/docs-mkdocs-blue)](https://kitokafor.github.io/romsort/) [![Downloads](https://img.shields.io/pypi/dm/romsort)](https://pypistats.org/packages/romsort) > **Note** > romsort only works with ROMs you dumped yourself or are otherwise legally allowed to have. It never downloads ROMs and never will, so please don't open issues asking for that. ## Features ## * Matches files by CRC32/SHA-1 against DAT files, so the filename doesn't matter at all * Renames to the canonical No-Intro / Redump name + Sorts into per-system folders (`snes/`, `megadrive/`, `psx/` ...) + **1G1R** mode: keeps one game per title, preferring your region order (`--regions EUR,USA,JPN`) - Handles `.zip` and `.7z` archives, and multi-track `.cue`/`.bin` sets - Dry-run by default :sunglasses: — you have to pass `--apply` to actually move anything Installation ------------ ```bash pipx install romsort # or, if you like living on the edge pipx install git+https://github.com/kitokafor/romsort ``` Needs Python 3.10 or newer. 7z support needs `py7zr`, which is an optional extra: `pipx install "romsort[7z]"`. ## Usage romsort scan ~/Roms/unsorted --dat-dir ~/Roms/dats romsort sort ~/Roms/unsorted ~/Roms/sorted --apply The first command only reads; it prints a report of what it found and what it *would* do. The second one actually moves files. Here's what the output looks like on a small folder: ~~~console $ romsort scan ./unsorted --dat-dir ./dats loaded 14 DAT files (38,212 entries) matched 212 / 230 files unknown 18 files (see romsort-unknown.txt) dupes 9 files (same SHA-1, different names) ~~~ ### Commands | command | what it does | safe? | |---|---|:---:| | `scan` | hash everything, match against the DATs, print a report | :white_check_mark: | | `sort` | move/rename matched files into `DEST//` | only with `--apply` | | `dedupe` | find duplicates, optionally delete them | :warning: with `--delete-dupes` | |`dat update`|download the latest DATs from your configured sources|:white_check_mark:| ### Config file romsort looks for `~/.config/romsort/config.yaml`. Every option can also be passed on the command line, the config file just saves typing. Files whose name ends in \_old or starts with \# are skipped, which is a leftover from my own folder structure and will probably become an option at some point. ```yaml # ~/.config/romsort/config.yaml dat_dir: ~/Roms/dats regions: [EUR, USA,JPN] one_game_one_rom: true systems: snes: {dat: "Nintendo - Super Nintendo Entertainment System", folder: snes} md: {dat: "Sega - Mega Drive - Genesis", folder: megadrive} psx: dat: Sony - PlayStation folder: psx prefer: [cue, chd] ignore: - "*.txt" - '*.nfo' - "[BIOS]*" ``` ## FAQ **Q: Why are some of my files "unknown"?** Usually one of these: 1) it's a bad dump or a hack (hacks aren't in No-Intro, by design) 2) it has a header the DAT doesn't expect. romsort strips iNES and SMC headers automatically, but not every weird copier header out there 3) you don't have the DAT for that system yet **Q: Can it convert `.bin`/`.cue` to `.chd`?**\ No, use `chdman` for that. romsort will happily sort the `.chd` files afterwards though. **Q: Does it work on Windows?** Probably? I don't have a Windows machine to test on. CI runs on Windows and the tests pass, which is about as much as I can promise. ## Roadmap - [x] No-Intro DATs - [x] Redump DATs (multi-track) - [ ] MAME (honestly, probably never, MAME sets are their own universe) - [ ] a tiny TUI for reviewing the "unknown" pile - [ ] with cover art from libretro-thumbnails? maybe ## Contributing PRs welcome! Please read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md "how to set up a dev environment") first, and run `make check` before pushing. If you're adding support for a new system, add a tiny *fake* DAT and fake ROM to `tests/fixtures/` (just a few bytes, __never__ real ROMs). *** Made with :heart: and too much coffee by Kit. Thanks to the [No-Intro][no-intro] and [Redump][redump] projects, without whom none of this would be possible, and to everyone who has ever filed a bug with a *useful* reproduction.[^1] ## License #### MIT, see [LICENSE](LICENSE). [^1]: you know who you are. there are four of you. [redump]: http://redump.org/ "Redump disc preservation" [no-intro]: https://no-intro.org

#!/usr/bin/env python3

# fmt: markdown
"""
dicegoblin
==========

A small Discord bot for our Thursday night D&D group.  It rolls dice, keeps track of whose turn it is to bring snacks, and nags everyone about the next session so we stop having the "wait, is it this week??" conversation every single Wednesday.

Setup:
1. Create an application + bot user in the Discord developer portal and copy the token.
2. `export DICEGOBLIN_TOKEN=...` (or put it in a `.env` file next to this script)
3. `python dicegoblin.py --init` writes a default `dicegoblin.yaml`, then edit the channel ids in it
4. `python dicegoblin.py` and leave it running somewhere (mine lives on the homelab NUC, in docker)

Requirements:
*   Python 3.10+ (I use `X | None` everywhere, sorry)
*   discord.py >= 2.3
*   PyYAML

A minimal config looks like this, everything else has defaults:

```yaml
prefix:   "!"
session: {day: thursday,   time: "19:30"}
channels:
    announcements: 123456789012345678
```

MIT licensed, do whatever you want with it. No warranty, *especially* not for natural 1s.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import datetime as dt
import logging
import os
import random
import re
import sys
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path

import discord
import yaml
from discord.ext import commands, tasks

log = logging.getLogger("dicegoblin")
CONFIG_PATH = Path(os.environ.get("DICEGOBLIN_CONFIG", Path(__file__).with_name("dicegoblin.yaml")))

# fmt: markdown
# ## Dice syntax
#
# The roller understands the usual tabletop notation. It's case-insensitive and whitespace is ignored:
#
# | expression | what it does |
# |---|:--|
# | `d20` | one twenty-sided die |
# | `4d6kh3` | roll four d6 and keep the highest three (stat rolls) |
# | `2d20kl1` | disadvantage, keep the lowest |
# | `1d8+3`, `2d6 - 1` | flat modifiers |
#
# Anything else gets a goblin-themed error message.  Exploding dice (`!`) are on the todo list, but honestly nobody has asked for them yet and the regex is already ugly enough.
DICE_RE = re.compile(r"^(?P<n>\d*)d(?P<sides>\d+)(?:k(?P<hl>[hl])(?P<keep>\d+))?(?P<mod>[+-]\d+)?$", re.IGNORECASE)  # fmt: skip


class DiceError(ValueError):
    pass


@dataclass
class Roll:
    expr: str
    dice: list[int]
    kept: list[int]
    modifier: int = 0

    @property
    def total(self) -> int:
        return sum(self.kept) + self.modifier

    def pretty(self) -> str:
        shown = [f"**{d}**" if d in self.kept else f"~~{d}~~" for d in self.dice]
        mod = f" {'+' if self.modifier >= 0 else '-'} {abs(self.modifier)}" if self.modifier else ""
        return f"`{self.expr}` → [{', '.join(shown)}]{mod} = **{self.total}**"


def roll(expr: str, rng: random.Random | None = None) -> Roll:
    rng = rng or random.SystemRandom()
    cleaned = expr.replace(" ", "").lower()
    m = DICE_RE.match(cleaned)
    if not m:
        raise DiceError(f"the goblin squints at `{expr}` and does not understand")
    n, sides = int(m["n"] or 1), int(m["sides"])
    if not 1 <= n <= 100 or sides not in (2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 20, 100):
        raise DiceError("the goblin only owns normal dice (and at most 100 of them)")
    dice = [rng.randint(1, sides) for _ in range(n)]
    kept = sorted(dice, reverse=m["hl"] != "l")
    if m["keep"]:
        kept = kept[: int(m["keep"])]
    return Roll(cleaned, dice, kept, int(m["mod"] or 0))


# fmt: off
DEFAULT_CONFIG = """\
# dicegoblin.yaml -- written by `dicegoblin.py --init`
prefix:   "!"
timezone: Europe/London
session:
    day: thursday
    time: "19:30"
    remind_hours_before: [24, 2]
channels: {announcements: 0, rolls: 0}   # right click a channel -> Copy Channel ID
snack_rota:
- Priya
- Tom
- "Mags"
- Dev
quiet: no
"""
# fmt: on


@dataclass
class Config:
    prefix: str = "!"
    timezone: str = "Europe/London"
    session_day: str = "thursday"
    session_time: str = "19:30"
    remind_hours_before: list[int] = field(default_factory=lambda: [24, 2])
    announcements: int = 0
    rolls: int = 0
    snack_rota: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    quiet: bool = False


def load_config(path: Path = CONFIG_PATH) -> Config:
    raw = yaml.safe_load(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) or {}
    session, channels = raw.get("session", {}), raw.get("channels", {})
    return Config(
        prefix=raw.get("prefix", "!"),
        timezone=raw.get("timezone", "Europe/London"),
        session_day=session.get("day", "thursday"),
        session_time=str(session.get("time", "19:30")),
        remind_hours_before=session.get("remind_hours_before", [24, 2]),
        announcements=int(channels.get("announcements", 0)),
        rolls=int(channels.get("rolls", 0)),
        snack_rota=list(raw.get("snack_rota", [])),
        quiet=bool(raw.get("quiet", False)),
    )


# fmt: markdown wrap=sentence
HELP_TEXT = """
**dicegoblin** knows the following commands. The prefix is configurable, these examples use `!`.

* `!roll 4d6kh3` – roll some dice. You can roll several at once: `!roll d20 d20 1d4+1`
* `!session` – when is the next session? The goblin does the timezone maths so you don't have to.
* `!snacks` – whose turn is it to bring snacks. `!snacks skip` moves on to the next person (e.g. if someone is ill).
*  `!goblin` – the goblin says something. It is not helpful.

Rolls go to the rolls channel if one is configured, otherwise they're posted right where you asked. Don't spam it please, Tom.
"""

# Sent once when the bot joins a server. Raw string because of the shrug.
# fmt: markdown
WELCOME = r"""
Hi! I'm the **dice goblin**. I roll dice, remember whose turn it is to bring snacks, and remind you about sessions.

Type `!help` to see what I can do. If something breaks, ¯\\\_(ツ)\_/¯ and poke whoever invited me.
"""

# fmt: markdown
REMINDER = """
:alarm_clock: **Session in {hours} hours!**
Starts {when}.   Bring your character sheet, your dice and, if it's your turn, __snacks__.
"""

GOBLIN_LINES = [
    "*rattles dice cup menacingly*",
    "the goblin has eaten one (1) d4. it was delicious.",
    "have you tried rolling higher",
]

intents = discord.Intents.default()
intents.message_content = True


class Goblin(commands.Bot):
    def __init__(self, config: Config) -> None:
        super().__init__(command_prefix=config.prefix, intents=intents, help_command=None)
        self.config = config
        self.snack_index = 0

    async def setup_hook(self) -> None:
        self.reminder_loop.start()

    def next_session(self, now: dt.datetime | None = None) -> dt.datetime:
        from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

        now = now or dt.datetime.now(ZoneInfo(self.config.timezone))
        days = ["monday", "tuesday", "wednesday", "thursday", "friday", "saturday", "sunday"]
        hour, minute = map(int, self.config.session_time.split(":"))
        when = now.replace(hour=hour, minute=minute, second=0, microsecond=0)
        when += dt.timedelta(days=(days.index(self.config.session_day.lower()) - now.weekday()) % 7)
        return when if when > now else when + dt.timedelta(days=7)

    @tasks.loop(minutes=10)
    async def reminder_loop(self) -> None:
        if self.config.quiet or not self.config.announcements:
            return
        when = self.next_session()
        hours_left = (when - dt.datetime.now(when.tzinfo)).total_seconds() / 3600
        for h in self.config.remind_hours_before:
            # the loop runs every 10 minutes, so only fire inside one 10 minute window
            if h - 1 / 6 < hours_left <= h and (channel := self.get_channel(self.config.announcements)):
                await channel.send(REMINDER.format(hours=h, when=discord.utils.format_dt(when, "F")))


def build_bot(config: Config) -> Goblin:
    bot = Goblin(config)

    @bot.command(name="roll", aliases=["r"])
    async def roll_cmd(ctx: commands.Context, *exprs: str) -> None:
        if not exprs:
            await ctx.reply("roll *what*? try `!roll d20`")
            return
        lines = []
        for e in exprs[:10]:
            try:
                lines.append(roll(e).pretty())
            except DiceError as err:
                lines.append(str(err))
        target = bot.get_channel(config.rolls) or ctx.channel
        await target.send(f"{ctx.author.mention}\n" + "\n".join(lines))

    @bot.command()
    async def snacks(ctx: commands.Context, action: str = "") -> None:
        rota = config.snack_rota or ["nobody, apparently"]
        bot.snack_index += action == "skip"
        await ctx.send(f"Snacks this week: **{rota[bot.snack_index % len(rota)]}**")

    @bot.command(name="help")
    async def help_cmd(ctx: commands.Context) -> None:
        await ctx.send(HELP_TEXT.replace("`!", f"`{config.prefix}"))

    @bot.event
    async def on_guild_join(guild: discord.Guild) -> None:
        if guild.system_channel:
            await guild.system_channel.send(WELCOME)

    return bot


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="dicegoblin", description="D&D helper bot")
    parser.add_argument("--init", action="store_true", help="write a default config and exit")
    parser.add_argument("--log-level", default=os.environ.get("DICEGOBLIN_LOG_LEVEL", "INFO"))
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    logging.basicConfig(level=args.log_level, format="%(asctime)s %(levelname)s %(name)s: %(message)s")
    if args.init:
        if CONFIG_PATH.exists():
            print(f"{CONFIG_PATH} already exists, not overwriting it", file=sys.stderr)
            return 1
        CONFIG_PATH.write_text(DEFAULT_CONFIG, encoding="utf-8")
        print(f"wrote {CONFIG_PATH}, now go and fill in the channel ids")
        return 0
    if not (token := os.environ.get("DICEGOBLIN_TOKEN")):
        print("DICEGOBLIN_TOKEN is not set", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    build_bot(load_config()).run(token, log_handler=None)
    return 0


# %% [markdown]
# Scratchpad: the cells below only do anything with `GOBLIN_SCRATCH=1` set, they're for poking at the roller in the VS Code interactive window.

# %%
#| label: scratch-distribution
#| eval:    false
#| tags: [scratch,dev]
#| fig-cap: "4d6kh3, 10k rolls"
if os.environ.get("GOBLIN_SCRATCH"):
    from collections import Counter

    counts = Counter(roll("4d6kh3", random.Random(42)).total for _ in range(10_000))
    for total in sorted(counts):
        print(f"{total:>2} {'#' * (counts[total] // 40)}")

# %%
#| label: scratch-parse
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: True
#| code-summary: 'show the parser checks'
if os.environ.get("GOBLIN_SCRATCH"):
    for e in ["d20", "4d6kh3", "2d20kl1", "1d8+3", "d7", "0d6", "101d6", "d20!"]:
        try:
            print(e, roll(e, random.Random(1)).pretty())
        except DiceError as err:
            print(e, "->", err)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

--- title: "Homelab Q3 2024: power, uptime & what broke" subtitle: 'A quarterly-ish review of the rack under the stairs' author: - name: Ines Ferreira url: https://ines.example.net date: 2024-10-06 date-modified: last-modified description: "Three months of smart-plug readings and Uptime Kuma exports, plus an honest accounting of every outage, including the two that were entirely my own fault." categories: [homelab, power, "self-hosting", uptime] format: html: toc: true toc-depth: 3 code-fold: true code-tools: True theme: [cosmo, custom.scss] fig-align: center execute: echo: false warning: false freeze: auto jupyter: python3 crossref: fig-prefix: Figure tbl-prefix: "Table" --- ## TL;DR {#sec-tldr} The rack drew **41.8 W on average** this quarter (down from 57 W in Q2), mostly because I finally retired the old Dell OptiPlex and moved everything onto the two N100 mini PCs. Uptime for the stuff the household actually notices (Home Assistant, Jellyfin, the Pi-hole) was above 99.5%, see @tbl-uptime, and the electricity bill impact is about €9 a month, which is less than a single streaming subscription so I'm calling that a win. ::: {.callout-note} All numbers come from two Shelly Plug S units logging to InfluxDB every 60 s, and from Uptime Kuma's SQLite database, which I copied off the NUC on 2024-10-01. The plugs claim ±1 W accuracy. I have not verified that and I don't really want to. ::: ![The rack under the stairs, mid-cable-management](images/rack-2024-09.jpg){#fig-rack fig-alt="A 10 inch rack on a shelf under the stairs with a patch panel, an 8 port switch, two mini PCs and a two-bay NAS, cables partly tidied with velcro" width="80%"} ```{python} #| label: setup #| include: false import pandas as pd import matplotlib.pyplot as plt power = pd.read_csv("data/power-q3.csv", parse_dates=["time"]) uptime = pd.read_csv("data/uptime-q3.csv") KWH_PRICE = 0.31 # EUR, fixed tariff until march ``` ## Power {#sec-power} @fig-power shows the daily average. The big dip in mid-August is the week the NAS spent at my parents' place for the offsite backup refresh, and the spike on 2024-09-14 is me running a Jellyfin library rescan *and* a ZFS scrub *and* compiling something, all at once, like an idiot. ```{python} #| label: fig-power #| fig-cap: "Daily average power draw of the rack, July to September 2024" #| fig-alt: "Line chart of daily mean watts, mostly flat around 40 W with a dip to 28 W in mid August and one spike to 71 W in mid September" #| fig-width: 8 #| fig-height: 3.5 daily = power.set_index("time").resample("D")["watts"].mean() ax = daily.plot(color="#7a5195") ax.set_ylabel("W") ax.set_xlabel("") plt.show() ``` The monthly cost works out as $$ \text{cost} = \bar{P} \cdot 24 \cdot 30 \cdot p_{\text{kWh}} \approx 41.8\,\text{W} \times 720\,\text{h} \times 0.31\,\text{€/kWh} $$ {#eq-cost} which is `{python} f"€{41.8 * 720 / 1000 * KWH_PRICE:.2f}"` per month. Plugging Q2's 57 W into @eq-cost gives roughly €12.70, so retiring the OptiPlex paid for one of the N100 boxes in about ~~two years~~ two and a half years. Ugh. The OptiPlex itself is now a very loud doorstop until I figure out what to do with it, suggestions welcome, no I will not run a Minecraft server on it. :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="55%"} ### Per device | Device | Avg W | Peak W | Notes | |:--|--:|---:|---| | N100 #1 (proxmox) | 11.2 | 24.9 | runs HA, Pi-hole, kuma | | N100 #2 (docker) | 9.8 | 31.0 | Jellyfin with QSV transcoding | | Synology DS220+ | 14.1 | 22.3 | spins down at night, *mostly* | | switch + AP | 6.7|7.1| PoE for the AP | : Average and peak power per device {#tbl-power} ::: ::: {.column width="5%"} ::: ::: {.column width="40%"} ::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"} The NAS disks spinning down saves about 4 W overnight. Getting `hdparm -S` to stick across DSM updates is left as an exercise for future me. ::: ::: :::: ## Uptime {#sec-uptime} ::: {.panel-tabset} ### Table ```{python} #| label: tbl-uptime #| tbl-cap: Uptime per service as measured by Uptime Kuma (HTTP checks every 60 s). Services marked with an asterisk are the ones anyone else in the house would notice. (uptime .assign(pct=lambda d: (100 * d.up / d.checks).round(2)) .sort_values("pct") [["service", "pct", "incidents"]]) ``` ### Chart ```{python} #| label: fig-uptime #| fig-cap: "Downtime minutes per service" #| fig-subcap: [ "All services", "Without the paperless outage"] #| layout-ncol: 2 for exclude in ([], ["paperless"]): d = uptime[~uptime.service.isin(exclude)] d.plot.barh(x="service", y="down_minutes", legend=False) plt.show() ``` ::: ## What broke {#sec-outages} 1. **Jul 12** – the Pi-hole died after an update and took DNS for the whole house with it. Household reaction: severe. Fix: a second Pi-hole on the NAS, see @sec-lessons. 2. **Aug 3** – paperless-ngx was down for ~19 hours because Redis ran out of memory; nobody noticed until I tried to find a receipt. 3. **Sep 14** – the power spike in @fig-power. Not an outage, just embarrassing. ::: {.callout-warning collapse="true"} ## The paperless outage, in detail Redis was configured with `maxmemory 64mb` because I copied a compose file from a blog post in 2021. paperless-ngx's task queue grew past that during a bulk import of ~1,400 scanned documents, Redis started evicting keys, and the consumer got stuck retrying the same task forever. The fix was one line. Finding it took an evening and a lot of {{< kbd Ctrl-C >}}. ::: ## Network, for reference ```{mermaid} %%| label: fig-network %%| fig-cap: "How things are wired (logically). The ISP router is in bridge mode." flowchart LR ISP[ISP router
bridge mode] --> OPN[OPNsense on N100 #1] OPN --> SW[8-port switch] SW --> AP[Wi-Fi AP] SW --> N2[N100 #2
docker] SW --> NAS[(DS220+)] OPN -. tailscale .-> PHONE[phones / laptop] ``` ## Lessons and next quarter {#sec-lessons} * Two DNS servers. Always two DNS servers. * Monitoring that nobody reads is not monitoring + Uptime Kuma now pushes to a Discord channel (the same server the dice bot lives on) + and to ntfy on my phone, but only for monitors tagged `critical` - Write down *why* a config value is what it is, future me does not remember[^redis] Plan for Q4: - [x] second Pi-hole - [ ] a UPS that actually talks to the NAS over USB (NUT) - [ ] move the Jellyfin metadata to the SSD - [ ] find out whether N100 #2 idles lower with `powertop --auto-tune` [^redis]: Case in point: the `maxmemory 64mb` line had a comment above it that just said `# important`. Thanks, 2021 me.

#' ---
#' title: "Greenhouse sensors: summer 2024"
#' author: "Jo"
#' date: "2024-09-28"
#' format:
#'   html:
#'     code-fold: true
#'     embed-resources: true
#' ---
#'
#' Quick look at the three ESPHome sensor nodes in the greenhouse (well, polytunnel). Data comes out of Home Assistant's long-term statistics via the InfluxDB export, see `export.flux` in this folder.

#| label: setup
#| message:   false
#| warning: FALSE
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(lubridate)

theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12))

# fmt: markdown
# ## Sensor nodes
#
# There are three nodes, all ESP32-C3 boards with an SHT31 for air temperature and humidity, plus a capacitive probe stuck in the soil of the middle bed:
#
# | node | location | notes |
# |------|----------|-------|
# | `gh-north` | north end, next to the door | gets a blast of cold air every time the door opens |
# | `gh-mid` | middle bed, 1m up | the "reference" one |
# | `gh-south` | south end, by the water butt | **in direct sun** from 2pm, afternoon readings are rubbish |
#
# The soil probes are uncalibrated, so I only ever look at the *relative* change.

#| label: load
#| cache: TRUE
readings <- read_csv("data/greenhouse-2024.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  mutate(
    time = with_tz(time, "Europe/London"),
    node = factor(node, levels = c("gh-north", "gh-mid", "gh-south"))
  ) |>
  filter(time >= ymd("2024-05-01"), time < ymd("2024-09-01"))

# the south node boot-looped for two days in July, drop those
readings <- readings |> filter(!(node == "gh-south" & between(time, ymd_hm("2024-07-09 10:00"), ymd_hm("2024-07-11 18:30"))))

# thresholds for the "hot days" counts below. Kept as YAML so the Home
# Assistant automation can read the exact same file.
thresholds_yaml <- r"(
hot:   35      # C, tomatoes stop setting fruit above this
cold: 4
humid: {max: 90, hours: 6}
alert_nodes: [gh-mid, "gh-north"]
)"
thresholds <- yaml::yaml.load(thresholds_yaml)

#| label: fig-daily
#| fig-cap: "Daily max/min air temperature per node. The grey band is the period with the shade net up."
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height:  4.5
#| fig-alt: Daily maximum and minimum temperature for three nodes from May to August, maximums mostly between 25 and 40 degrees
daily <- readings |>
  mutate(day = as_date(time)) |>
  group_by(node, day) |>
  summarise(tmax = max(temp_c, na.rm = TRUE), tmin = min(temp_c, na.rm = TRUE), rh = mean(rh, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

ggplot(daily, aes(day)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = ymd("2024-07-01"), xmax = ymd("2024-08-15"), ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, alpha = 0.1) +
  geom_line(aes(y = tmax, colour = node)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = tmin, colour = node), linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = thresholds$hot, colour = "firebrick", linewidth = 0.3) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "°C", colour = NULL)

# fmt: markdown
# ### Did the shade net help?
#
# Short answer: yes, a bit. Long answer: the comparison is confounded by July being cooler than June anyway, so the raw before/after numbers overstate it.  Comparing `gh-mid` against the outdoor sensor on the shed (not in this dataset, it's in a different InfluxDB bucket because past me is an idiot) the gap between inside and outside dropped from roughly 9 degrees to roughly 6.
#
# + days over 35C before the net: lots
# + days over 35C with the net: fewer
#    + but still some, mostly at the south end
# + tomatoes: did not care either way, they were delicious

#| label: tbl-hot-days
#| tbl-cap: Days per month where the max temperature went over the "hot" threshold, or the min went under the "cold" one
#| layout-ncol: 1
hot_days <- daily |>
  mutate(month = month(day, label = TRUE)) |>
  group_by(node, month) |>
  summarise(hot = sum(tmax > thresholds$hot), cold = sum(tmin < thresholds$cold), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = node, values_from = c(hot, cold), values_fill = 0)
knitr::kable(hot_days)

# fmt: markdown
#' ## Humidity
#'
#' Humidity is the one I actually care about, because of blight.  Anything above 90% for more than ~6 hours in a row counts as a "blight risk" period in the plot below, which is the same rule the Home Assistant automation uses to send me a notification and open the vent.
#'
#' * `gh-mid` is the one the automation listens to
#' * the vent motor is a cheap linear actuator, so "open" means "open-ish"

#| label: fig-humidity
#| fig-cap: "Daily mean relative humidity"
#| fig-subcap:
#| - "All nodes"
#| - 'gh-mid only'
#| layout-ncol: 2
ggplot(daily, aes(day, rh, colour = node)) + geom_line() + geom_hline(yintercept = thresholds$humid$max, linetype = "dotted")
ggplot(filter(daily, node == "gh-mid"), aes(day, rh)) + geom_col(fill = "steelblue")

# fmt: markdown
summary_md <- "
## Greenhouse summary, summer 2024

The hottest day was **%s** at %.1f °C (node `%s`). There were %d days over %d °C in total, most of them in June before the shade net went up.

* humidity alerts: %d
* sensor dropouts longer than an hour: %d
"

hottest <- daily |> slice_max(tmax, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
msg <- sprintf(
  summary_md,
  format(hottest$day, "%d %B"), hottest$tmax, as.character(hottest$node),
  sum(daily$tmax > thresholds$hot), thresholds$hot,
  0L, 2L
)
writeLines(msg, "out/summary.md")

# fmt: markdown wrap=sentence
ntfy_message <- r"[
Greenhouse report for **summer 2024** is ready! Hottest node was `gh-south`, as always. The HTML version is on the NAS: <http://nas.lan/reports/greenhouse-2024.html>

- tomatoes: 14.2 kg (approx., the kitchen scale is not great)
- chillies: lots vs. last year's none. Next year: fewer chillies.
]"
httr2::request("https://ntfy.sh/jo-greenhouse") |>
  httr2::req_headers(Markdown = "yes", Title = "Greenhouse report") |>
  httr2::req_body_raw(ntfy_message) |>
  httr2::req_perform()

#| label: session
#| echo: false
#| include: !expr interactive()
sessionInfo()

---
title: "Is the dice goblin cursed?"
subtitle:   "A totally serious statistical investigation of 4,000+ d20 rolls"
author: "Priya S."
date: "`r format(Sys.Date(), '%d %B %Y')`"
output:
    html_document:
        toc: yes
        toc_float: true
        code_folding: hide
        theme: flatly
params:
  bot_log: "data/rolls.csv"
  min_rolls: 30
editor_options:
  markdown:
    wrap: sentence
  chunk_output_type: console
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(readr)
rolls <- read_csv(params$bot_log)
```

## Background

Our D&D group uses a Discord bot (the "dice goblin", written by Ines, source at https://github.com/inesferreira/dicegoblin) for every single roll. Over the last few months Tom has become convinced that the goblin hates him specifically. His evidence: he rolled three natural 1s in a row on Thursday 14 March, i.e. the night his paladin nearly died. Is that suspicious? Not really! The probability of three 1s in a row on a fair d20 is 1 in 8000, which sounds tiny, but we roll a *lot* of dice. So I decided to settle this properly, with data vs. with yelling. Mr. Whiskers (Ines's cat, who walks across her keyboard during every session) is not considered a confounder.

## The data

The bot logs every roll to a CSV file (`rolls.csv`) with the user, the expression and each individual die. I only kept plain `d20` rolls, i.e. no advantage or disadvantage, because `2d20kh1` is not uniform (that's the whole point of it). That leaves `r nrow(rolls)` rolls from 6 players over 23 sessions. Session No. 5 is missing because the bot was down; Ines says it was "a Docker thing".

```{r d20-only}
d20 <- rolls %>% filter(expr == "d20") %>% mutate(face = as.integer(result))
nrow(d20)
```

## Is the die fair overall?

```{r overall-histogram, echo=FALSE, fig.cap="Distribution of all plain d20 rolls. The dashed line is the expected count for a fair die.", fig.width=8, fig.height=4}
expected <- nrow(d20) / 20
ggplot(d20, aes(face)) +
  geom_bar(fill = "#58508d") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = expected, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:20) +
  labs(x = "Face", y = "Count")
```

A chi-squared goodness-of-fit test is the obvious first step. With 20 faces there are 19 degrees of freedom, and the test statistic came out at `r round(chisq.test(table(d20$face))$statistic, 1)` with p = `r signif(chisq.test(table(d20$face))$p.value, 2)`. In plain English: no evidence at all that the die is unfair. The most common face was 17 and the least common was 9. Neither of those is a 1, Tom.

## But what about Tom specifically?

Fine. Let's look at each player separately (see Fig. 2 below). There is an obvious multiple-comparisons problem here, e.g. with six players the chance that at least one of them looks "unlucky" at the 5% level is approx. 26%, so I used a Bonferroni correction. Dr. Google tells me that's conservative. That is fine, conservative is what we want when the alternative hypothesis is "the goblin is cursed".

```{r per-player, fig.cap="Mean roll per player with 95% intervals. A fair d20 has a mean of 10.5."}
d20 %>%
  group_by(user) %>%
  filter(n() >= params$min_rolls) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), mean = mean(face), se = sd(face) / sqrt(n)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(reorder(user, mean), mean)) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = mean - 1.96 * se, ymax = mean + 1.96 * se)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 10.5, linetype = "dotted") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Mean d20 roll")
```

Results, in no particular order:

* **Tom** averaged 10.2 over 731 rolls. That is below 10.5! It is also completely normal. His three 1s in a row did happen, but so did Mags's four 20s in two sessions and nobody complained about that.
* **Priya** (me) averaged 10.9. I would like it noted that I did not tamper with the bot. I don't even know Python.
* **Dev** only has 88 rolls because he joined in May, so his interval is huge. Welcome, Dev!
* Everyone else was within 0.4 of 10.5.

| player | rolls | mean | nat 1s | nat 20s |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Tom | 731 | 10.2 | 41 | 33 |
| Priya | 702 | 10.9 | 30 | 38 |
| Mags | 688 | 10.6 | 33 | 37 |

## Streaks

The streak question is more interesting. How often should we see three 1s in a row from *someone* at the table? I simulated 10,000 campaigns of the same length as ours (same number of sessions, same rolls per player per session) with `sample(1:20, replace = TRUE)` and counted how many had at least one triple-1 streak. The answer was 41%. So, roughly a coin flip. Tom's streak is about as surprising as getting heads.[^sim]

```{r streaks, cache=TRUE}
set.seed(2024)
sim <- replicate(10000, {
  runs <- rle(sample(1:20, nrow(d20), replace = TRUE) == 1)
  any(runs$lengths[runs$values] >= 3)
})
mean(sim)
```

> Tom, reading a draft of this: "ok but what if the goblin knows when it's me". He then asked whether the bot could be "re-seeded with good vibes". It cannot. The bot uses `random.SystemRandom()`, which reads from the operating system, so there is nothing to re-seed!

## Conclusions

1. The dice goblin is not cursed. The `SystemRandom` source it uses (see `dicegoblin.py`, line 60 or so) is about as fair as it gets.
2. Tom is not cursed either. He is just a person who remembers his bad rolls. We all are!
3. Humans are terrible at judging randomness. This is well documented, see e.g. Tversky and Kahneman (1971), and it is also documented in every D&D group chat ever.

Next steps? I'd like to check whether people roll differently on their phone vs. on desktop (they shouldn't, the bot doesn't know), and whether rolls are more likely to get re-rolled ("my cat stepped on enter!!") after a low result. That second one isn't about the dice at all, it's about us. *Spoiler: it's Tom. It's always Tom.*

[^sim]: The simulation ignores that some rolls happen in quick bursts (e.g. fireball damage), which makes streaks slightly *more* likely in practice. So if anything, 41% is an underestimate. Sorry, Tom.

---

*Data: 23 sessions, Jan.–Jun. 2024. Code and data are at https://github.com/priyas/goblin-stats if you want to check my work. No goblins were harmed.*

#!/usr/bin/env python3

# fmt: markdown
"""
dicegoblin
==========

A small Discord bot for our Thursday night D&D group.  It rolls dice, keeps track of whose turn it is to bring snacks, and nags everyone about the next session so we stop having the "wait, is it this week??" conversation every single Wednesday.

Setup:
1. Create an application + bot user in the Discord developer portal and copy the token.
2. `export DICEGOBLIN_TOKEN=...` (or put it in a `.env` file next to this script)
3. `python dicegoblin.py --init` writes a default `dicegoblin.yaml`, then edit the channel ids in it
4. `python dicegoblin.py` and leave it running somewhere (mine lives on the homelab NUC, in docker)

Requirements:
*   Python 3.10+ (I use `X | None` everywhere, sorry)
*   discord.py >= 2.3 and PyYAML

A minimal config looks like this, everything else has defaults:

```yaml
prefix:   "!"
session: {day: thursday,   time: "19:30"}
channels:
    announcements: 123456789012345678
```

MIT licensed, do whatever you want with it. No warranty, *especially* not for natural 1s.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import datetime as dt
import os
import random
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

import discord
import yaml
from discord.ext import commands, tasks

CONFIG_PATH = Path(os.environ.get("DICEGOBLIN_CONFIG", Path(__file__).with_name("dicegoblin.yaml")))

# fmt: markdown
# ## Dice syntax
#
# The roller understands the usual tabletop notation. It's case-insensitive and whitespace is ignored:
#
# | expression | what it does |
# |---|:--|
# | `d20` | one twenty-sided die |
# | `4d6kh3` | roll four d6 and keep the highest three (stat rolls) |
# | `2d20kl1` | disadvantage, keep the lowest |
# | `1d8+3`, `2d6 - 1` | flat modifiers |
#
# Anything else gets a goblin-themed error message.  Exploding dice (`!`) are on the todo list, but honestly nobody has asked for them yet and the regex is already ugly enough.
DICE_RE = re.compile(r"^(?P<n>\d*)d(?P<sides>\d+)(?:k(?P<hl>[hl])(?P<keep>\d+))?(?P<mod>[+-]\d+)?$", re.IGNORECASE)  # fmt: skip


class DiceError(ValueError):
    pass


def roll(expr: str, rng: random.Random | None = None) -> tuple[int, str]:
    """Roll `expr` and return (total, pretty string for discord)."""
    rng = rng or random.SystemRandom()
    cleaned = expr.replace(" ", "").lower()
    m = DICE_RE.match(cleaned)
    if not m:
        raise DiceError(f"the goblin squints at `{expr}` and does not understand")
    n, sides = int(m["n"] or 1), int(m["sides"])
    if not 1 <= n <= 100 or sides not in (2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 20, 100):
        raise DiceError("the goblin only owns normal dice (and at most 100 of them)")
    dice = [rng.randint(1, sides) for _ in range(n)]
    kept = sorted(dice, reverse=m["hl"] != "l")[: int(m["keep"] or n)]
    mod = int(m["mod"] or 0)
    total = sum(kept) + mod
    shown = ", ".join(f"**{d}**" if d in kept else f"~~{d}~~" for d in dice)
    return total, f"`{cleaned}` → [{shown}]{f' {mod:+d}' if mod else ''} = **{total}**"


# fmt: off
DEFAULT_CONFIG = """\
# dicegoblin.yaml -- written by `dicegoblin.py --init`
prefix:   "!"
timezone: Europe/London
session:
    day: thursday
    time: "19:30"     # keep the quotes, PyYAML reads 19:30 as a number otherwise
    remind_hours_before: [24, 2]
channels: {announcements: 0, rolls: 0}   # right click a channel -> Copy Channel ID
snack_rota:
- Priya
- Tom
- "Mags"
- Dev
quiet: no
"""

#!/usr/bin/env python3

# fmt: markdown
"""
dicegoblin
==========

A small Discord bot for our Thursday night D&D group.  It rolls dice, keeps track of whose turn it is to bring snacks, and nags everyone about the next session so we stop having the "wait, is it this week??" conversation every single Wednesday.

Setup:
1. Create an application + bot user in the Discord developer portal and copy the token.
2. `export DICEGOBLIN_TOKEN=...` (or put it in a `.env` file next to this script)
3. `python dicegoblin.py --init` writes a default `dicegoblin.yaml`, then edit the channel ids in it
4. `python dicegoblin.py` and leave it running somewhere (mine lives on the homelab NUC, in docker)

Requirements:
*   Python 3.10+ (I use `X | None` everywhere, sorry)
*   discord.py >= 2.3 and PyYAML

A minimal config looks like this, everything else has defaults:

```yaml
prefix:   "!"
session: {day: thursday,   time: "19:30"}
channels:
    announcements: 123456789012345678
```

MIT licensed, do whatever you want with it. No warranty, *especially* not for natural 1s.
"""

import argparse
import datetime as dt
import os
import random
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

import discord
import yaml
from discord.ext import commands, tasks

CONFIG_PATH = Path(os.environ.get("DICEGOBLIN_CONFIG", Path(__file__).with_name("dicegoblin.yaml")))

# fmt: markdown
# ## Dice syntax
#
# The roller understands the usual tabletop notation. It's case-insensitive and whitespace is ignored:
#
# | expression | what it does |
# |---|:--|
# | `d20` | one twenty-sided die |
# | `4d6kh3` | roll four d6 and keep the highest three (stat rolls) |
# | `2d20kl1` | disadvantage, keep the lowest |
# | `1d8+3`, `2d6 - 1` | flat modifiers |
#
# Anything else gets a goblin-themed error message.  Exploding dice (`!`) are on the todo list, but honestly nobody has asked for them yet and the regex is already ugly enough.
DICE_RE = re.compile(r"^(?P<n>\d*)d(?P<sides>\d+)(?:k(?P<hl>[hl])(?P<keep>\d+))?(?P<mod>[+-]\d+)?$", re.IGNORECASE)  # fmt: skip


class DiceError(ValueError):
    pass


def roll(expr: str, rng: random.Random | None = None) -> tuple[int, str]:
    rng = rng or random.SystemRandom()
    cleaned = expr.replace(" ", "").lower()
    m = DICE_RE.match(cleaned)
    if not m:
        raise DiceError(f"the goblin squints at `{expr}` and does not understand")
    n, sides = int(m["n"] or 1), int(m["sides"])
    if not 1 <= n <= 100 or sides not in (2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 20, 100):
        raise DiceError("the goblin only owns normal dice (and at most 100 of them)")
    dice = [rng.randint(1, sides) for _ in range(n)]
    kept = sorted(dice, reverse=m["hl"] != "l")[: int(m["keep"] or n)]
    mod = int(m["mod"] or 0)
    total = sum(kept) + mod
    shown = ", ".join(f"**{d}**" if d in kept else f"~~{d}~~" for d in dice)
    return total, f"`{cleaned}` → [{shown}]{f' {mod:+d}' if mod else ''} = **{total}**"


# fmt: off
DEFAULT_CONFIG = """\
# dicegoblin.yaml -- written by `dicegoblin.py --init`
prefix:   "!"
timezone: Europe/London
session:
    day: thursday
    time: "19:30"     # keep the quotes, PyYAML reads 19:30 as a number otherwise
    remind_hours_before: [24, 2]
channels: {announcements: 0, rolls: 0}   # right click a channel -> Copy Channel ID
snack_rota:
- Priya
- Tom
- "Mags"
- Dev
quiet: no
"""
# fmt: on

# fmt: markdown wrap=sentence
HELP_TEXT = """
**dicegoblin** knows the following commands. The prefix is configurable, these examples use `!`.

* `!roll 4d6kh3` – roll some dice. You can roll several at once: `!roll d20 d20 1d4+1`
* `!session` – when is the next session? The goblin does the timezone maths so you don't have to.
* `!snacks` – whose turn is it to bring snacks. `!snacks skip` moves on to the next person (e.g. if someone is ill).
*  `!goblin` – the goblin says something. It is not helpful.

Rolls go to the rolls channel if one is configured, otherwise they're posted right where you asked. Don't spam it please, Tom.
"""

# Sent once when the bot joins a server. Raw string because of the shrug.
# fmt: markdown
WELCOME = r"""
Hi! I'm the **dice goblin**. I roll dice, remember whose turn it is to bring snacks, and remind you about sessions.

Type `!help` to see what I can do. If something breaks, ¯\\\_(ツ)\_/¯ and poke whoever invited me.
"""

# fmt: markdown
REMINDER = """
:alarm_clock: **Session in {hours} hours!**
Starts {when}.   Bring your character sheet, your dice and, if it's your turn, __snacks__.
"""


class Goblin(commands.Bot):
    def __init__(self, cfg: dict) -> None:
        super().__init__(command_prefix=cfg["prefix"], intents=discord.Intents.all(), help_command=None)
        self.cfg, self.snack_index = cfg, 0

    async def setup_hook(self) -> None:
        self.reminder_loop.start()

    def next_session(self) -> dt.datetime:
        now = dt.datetime.now(ZoneInfo(self.cfg["timezone"]))
        day = ["monday", "tuesday", "wednesday", "thursday", "friday", "saturday", "sunday"].index(self.cfg["session"]["day"])
        hour, minute = map(int, str(self.cfg["session"]["time"]).split(":"))
        when = now.replace(hour=hour, minute=minute, second=0, microsecond=0) + dt.timedelta(days=(day - now.weekday()) % 7)
        return when if when > now else when + dt.timedelta(days=7)

    @tasks.loop(minutes=10)
    async def reminder_loop(self) -> None:
        channel = self.get_channel(self.cfg["channels"]["announcements"])
        when = self.next_session()
        hours_left = (when - dt.datetime.now(when.tzinfo)).total_seconds() / 3600
        for h in self.cfg["session"].get("remind_hours_before", [24, 2]):
            # the loop runs every 10 minutes, so only fire inside one 10 minute window
            if channel and not self.cfg["quiet"] and h - 1 / 6 < hours_left <= h:
                await channel.send(REMINDER.format(hours=h, when=discord.utils.format_dt(when, "F")))


def build_bot(cfg: dict) -> Goblin:
    bot = Goblin(cfg)

    @bot.command(name="roll", aliases=["r"])
    async def roll_cmd(ctx: commands.Context, *exprs: str) -> None:
        lines = []
        for e in exprs[:10] or ["d20"]:
            try:
                lines.append(roll(e)[1])
            except DiceError as err:
                lines.append(str(err))
        target = bot.get_channel(cfg["channels"]["rolls"]) or ctx.channel
        await target.send(f"{ctx.author.mention}\n" + "\n".join(lines))

    @bot.command()
    async def snacks(ctx: commands.Context, action: str = "") -> None:
        bot.snack_index += action == "skip"
        rota = cfg["snack_rota"] or ["nobody, apparently"]
        await ctx.send(f"Snacks this week: **{rota[bot.snack_index % len(rota)]}**")

    @bot.command(name="help")
    async def help_cmd(ctx: commands.Context) -> None:
        await ctx.send(HELP_TEXT.replace("`!", f"`{cfg['prefix']}"))

    @bot.event
    async def on_guild_join(guild: discord.Guild) -> None:
        if guild.system_channel:
            await guild.system_channel.send(WELCOME)

    return bot


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="dicegoblin", description="D&D helper bot")
    parser.add_argument("--init", action="store_true", help="write a default config and exit")
    if parser.parse_args().init:
        if CONFIG_PATH.exists():
            sys.exit(f"{CONFIG_PATH} already exists, not overwriting it")
        CONFIG_PATH.write_text(DEFAULT_CONFIG, encoding="utf-8")
        print(f"wrote {CONFIG_PATH}, now go and fill in the channel ids")
        return 0
    if not (token := os.environ.get("DICEGOBLIN_TOKEN")):
        sys.exit("DICEGOBLIN_TOKEN is not set")
    cfg = yaml.safe_load(DEFAULT_CONFIG) | (yaml.safe_load(CONFIG_PATH.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) or {})
    build_bot(cfg).run(token)
    return 0

## TL;DR {#sec-tldr}

The rack drew **41.8 W on average** this quarter (down from 57 W in Q2), mostly because I finally retired the old Dell OptiPlex and moved everything onto the two N100 mini PCs. Uptime for the stuff the household actually notices (Home Assistant, Jellyfin, the Pi-hole) was above 99.5%, see @tbl-uptime, and the electricity bill impact is about €9 a month, which is less than a single streaming subscription so I'm calling that a win.

::: {.callout-note}
All numbers come from two Shelly Plug S units logging to InfluxDB every 60 s, and from Uptime Kuma's SQLite database, which I copied off the NUC on 2024-10-01.  
The plugs claim ±1 W accuracy. I have not verified that and I don't really want to.
:::

> He then asked whether the bot could be "re-seeded with good vibes". It cannot. The bot uses `random.SystemRandom()`, which reads from the operating system, so there is nothing to re-seed!

## Conclusions

1. The dice goblin is not cursed. The `SystemRandom` source it uses (see `dicegoblin.py`, line 60 or so) is about as fair as it gets.
2. Tom is not cursed either. He is just a person who remembers his bad rolls. We all are!
3. Humans are terrible at judging randomness. This is well documented, see e.g. Tversky and Kahneman (1971), and it is also documented in every D&D group chat ever.

Next steps? I'd like to check whether people roll differently on their phone vs. on desktop (they shouldn't, the bot doesn't know), and whether rolls are more likely to get re-rolled ("my cat stepped on enter!!") after a low result. That second one isn't about the dice at all, it's about us. *Spoiler: it's Tom. It's always Tom.*

[^sim]: The simulation ignores that some rolls happen in quick bursts (e.g. fireball damage), which makes streaks slightly *more* likely in practice. So if anything, 41% is an underestimate. Sorry, Tom.
